That page exists (`docs/site/best-practices.md`, published on GH Pages), but no MCP tool exposes it. So today: an MCP client asking "what are best practices for creating a suite/check?" gets an answer only from the LLM's own knowledge/training (or whatever's baked into tool docstrings) — it cannot fetch `best-practices.md` itself, since there's no tool wired to read docs content, and MCP tools don't have open internet/URL access by default.

To make that actually work, you'd need a new read-only tool (e.g. `get_best_practices` or a generic `get_docs_page`) that reads the markdown from the repo/site and returns it as a resource. That's a small, clean addition — read-only, no authz complexity, similar shape to the other read tools. Want me to scope that out as an issue, or are you just checking current behavior?
What do you suggest?

I'd expose the docs as MCP **resources**, not another tool — FastMCP supports `@mcp.resource` for exactly this (static reference content, not an action to invoke), so it stays separate from the curated 46-tool surface and doesn't need RBAC/authz plumbing since it's public docs anyway. Main tradeoff: not every MCP client surfaces resources as prominently as tools, so some clients might still miss it unless they proactively browse resources.

If you want it to work as reliably as a tool call (client explicitly asks, always gets it), a thin read-only tool like `get_best_practices` is the safer bet at the cost of one more entry in the tool list. Given the docs are already public on GH Pages, either way it's a small addition — want me to spec it out as an issue?

# Model Context Protocol (MCP)

Let your AI agents interact with the Stripe API by using our MCP server.

Read this page in your terminal: [install the Stripe CLI](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/install) (v1.43.3+) and run `stripe docs`. [Reference](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/docs)

## Start here: Integrate with Stripe using skills and plugins

Stripe provides skills and plugins for agents to build faster and more accurately. See [Agent skills](https://docs.stripe.com/skills.md) for more information.

**Quickstart**: Install the Stripe CLI with `npm install -g @stripe/cli` and run `stripe agent setup`.

The Stripe Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides tools that AI agents can use to interact with the Stripe API and search Stripe’s knowledge base, including documentation and support articles.

## Set up Stripe MCP with a plugin  (Recommended)

[Agent plugins](https://docs.stripe.com/agents/plugin.md) for Stripe automatically configure the Stripe MCP server, install our [skills](https://docs.stripe.com/skills.md), and make sure they’re up-to-date. You get our latest capabilities without configuration or maintenance.

To install, run:

```bash
npm install -g @stripe/cli@latest
stripe agent setup
```

This command automatically detects which agents you use, and runs the applicable commands.

## Manually set up Stripe MCP 

If your MCP client doesn’t support [agent plugins](https://docs.stripe.com/agents/plugin.md) for Stripe, or you prefer to configure the Stripe MCP server and install the skills manually, follow these instructions:

#### Cursor

[Install in Cursor](cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=stripe&REDACTED%3D)

Select **Install in Cursor** to open Cursor and add the Stripe MCP server. To configure it manually, add the following configuration to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`.

For more information, see [Cursor’s MCP documentation](https://docs.cursor.com/context/model-context-protocol).

```json
{
 "mcpServers": {
   "stripe": {
     "url": "https://mcp.stripe.com"
   }
 }
}
```

#### Claude Code

Run the following command to add the Stripe MCP server to Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http stripe https://mcp.stripe.com/
```

After you add the server, authenticate Stripe with OAuth.

```bash
claude /mcp
```

To authenticate with a restricted API key instead of OAuth, use the `--header` option:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http stripe https://mcp.stripe.com/ --header 'Authorization: Bearer <<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>'
```

For more information, see [Claude Code MCP documentation](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/mcp#configure-mcp-servers).

#### ChatGPT and Codex

### ChatGPT

With a ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, or Education account, you can [install the Stripe plugin in ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_connector_690ab09fa43c8191bca40280e4563238).

### Codex CLI

To use the Stripe MCP server with the Codex CLI, add it to your `~/.codex/config.toml` file. To learn more, see the OpenAI [Codex MCP documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp).

```toml
[mcp_servers.stripe]
url = "https://mcp.stripe.com"
```

After you add the server, authenticate Stripe with OAuth.

```bash
codex mcp login stripe
```

To authenticate with a restricted API key instead of OAuth, set `bearer_token_env_var` to the name of an environment variable that holds your key. In this example, `STRIPE_API_KEY` is a placeholder, replace it with the actual name of your environment variable.

```toml
[mcp_servers.stripe]
url = "https://mcp.stripe.com"
bearer_token_env_var = "STRIPE_API_KEY" # Replace with the name of your environment variable
```

#### Other

### Install in VS Code

[Install in VS Code](https://vscode.dev/redirect/mcp/install?name=stripe&config=%7B%22type%22%3A%22http%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.stripe.com%22%7D)

Select **Install in VS Code** to open VS Code and add the Stripe MCP server. To configure it manually, add the following configuration to `.vscode/mcp.json` in your workspace.

See the [VS Code MCP documentation](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/chat/mcp-servers) for more information.

```json
{
 "servers": {
   "stripe": {
     "type": "http",
     "url": "https://mcp.stripe.com"
   }
 }
}
```

### Install from another MCP client

MCP is an open protocol supported by many clients. Follow your client’s MCP setup instructions and use `https://mcp.stripe.com` as the server URL.

Use OAuth when your client supports it. If your client doesn’t support OAuth, use a [restricted API key](https://docs.stripe.com/keys/restricted-api-keys.md) as a bearer token in the `Authorization` header. For example, if your client accepts a `headers` property, use the following configuration:

```json
{
 "stripe": {
   "url": "https://mcp.stripe.com",
   "headers": {
     "Authorization": "Bearer <restricted_api_key>"
   }
 }
}
```

## Manage MCP access and sessions 

Stripe’s MCP server uses OAuth to authorize clients according to the [MCP specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/authorization#2-1-1-oauth-grant-types). OAuth lets you grant and revoke access without sharing an API key with the client.

When you connect an MCP client, it opens Stripe’s OAuth consent page. Use this page to authorize the client to access your Stripe data. After you authorize an MCP client with OAuth, you can manage its session in the Stripe Dashboard.

If your organization manages your device or network, your IT administrator might block connections to external MCP servers. When the Stripe MCP server doesn’t connect in a managed environment, ask your IT department to allow `mcp.stripe.com`.

### Manage your sessions 

Your authorized MCP clients appear under **OAuth sessions** in your [user settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/user). To revoke a session:

1. Find the client in the **OAuth sessions** list.
2. Click the overflow menu (⋯).
3. Select **Revoke access**.

### Manage sessions as an administrator 

To view or revoke another user’s sessions, your role must include permissions to manage team members and OAuth sessions. The **Administrator** role includes these permissions.

1. Open [Team and security](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/team) in the Dashboard.
2. Select the team member you want to manage.
3. Find the **OAuth sessions** table.
4. To revoke one session, click its overflow menu and select **Revoke access**. To revoke every listed session, select **Revoke all**.

Session management applies only to the account or organization and environment—live mode or a sandbox—that you’re currently viewing. Revoking a session removes access only within that scope. The session remains active for accounts outside your current scope.

When you view an organization, the **Accounts** column shows the accounts associated with each session.

### Manage MCP access 

Administrators can [manage MCP access](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/mcp) in the Dashboard. Configure access separately for live mode and sandbox environments.

## Tools

The server exposes the following [MCP tools](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/tools).

Enable human confirmation of tools and exercise caution when using the Stripe MCP with other servers to avoid prompt injection attacks. If you have feedback or want to see more tools, email us at [mcp@stripe.com](mailto:mcp@stripe.com).

| Resource | Tool | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **API tools** | `stripe_api_search` | Search for Stripe API methods by keyword |
| `stripe_api_details` | Get detailed parameter information for a specific Stripe API method. |
| `stripe_api_read` | Read data with any Stripe API `GET` method |
| `stripe_api_write` | Write data with any Stripe API `POST`, `PATCH`, `PUT` and `DELETE` method |
| **Account** | `get_stripe_account_info` | [Retrieve account](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/retrieve.md) |
| **Analytics** (Private preview) | `stripe_analytics` | Query metrics, run SQL against reporting tables, or run pre-built templates |
| `show_metric_app` | Visually displays a Stripe analytics metric in a time-series line chart |
| `list_metrics` | List all available metrics that you can use with `stripe_analytics`, `explain_metric`, `show_metric_app`, and related tools |
| `explain_metric` | Fetch the Sigma query used to calculate a metric |
| `metric_drilldown` | View row-level data for a metric with a specific time range filter |
| **Refund** | `create_refund` | [Create refund](https://docs.stripe.com/api/refunds/create.md) |

| `send_stripe_mcp_feedback` | Submit feedback from user or agent about Stripe MCP server tools |

Found a clear real-world data point: **Stripe's MCP server** does exactly this — it has a dedicated `search_stripe_documentation` tool (search-based, not a raw dump) plus `stripe_implementation_planner`, a guided-workflow tool built on top of the docs to walk an agent through a task. GitHub's MCP server, by contrast, exposes repo content as a **resource** (passive, not an invoked action) rather than a tool. And you already trust this exact pattern — `context7` in DataQ's own `.mcp.json` is a search/query tool over external library docs.

So the field splits into two mechanisms, and the right one depends on corpus size:

**Option A — MCP resource** (`@mcp.resource`, FastMCP supports this)
Register `best-practices.md` (and maybe `feature-matrix.md`, `mcp-setup.md`) as static resources. Cheapest to build, matches GitHub's pattern for static content. Downside: not every client surfaces resources as proactively as tools — some only pull them in if the user or client explicitly browses resources.

**Option B — A scoped lookup tool**, e.g. `get_doc(page: "best-practices" | "feature-matrix" | ...)`
Guarantees any client can explicitly fetch it on request ("what are best practices for creating a suite?" → tool call, reliable). This is the Stripe shape, minus search — DataQ's docs corpus is a handful of pages, so an enum-scoped lookup beats building a search index you don't need yet.

**Option C — Full search tool** (Stripe's actual `search_stripe_documentation` shape)
Only worth it once the docs corpus is large enough that keyword search beats a flat page-name enum. Overkill for DataQ today.

**Option D — Do nothing separate**, lean on tool docstrings only
This is what the MCP honesty pass already invested in — docstrings carry operational caveats. But it doesn't cover conceptual guidance that isn't tied to one tool call (e.g. "how should I structure a suite" isn't inside any single tool's docstring).

My pick: **B now**, with a clean path to **C** later if the docs grow. It's a small, read-only, no-authz addition — same shape as the rest of DataQ's read tools — and doesn't depend on client-specific resource support.

Not reliably as designed so far — because there's no single "compliance" page to fetch. It's fragmented across five separate docs: `sub-processors.md`, `dpia-input-sheet.md`, `data-subject-rights-runbook.md`, `breach-notification-runbook.md`, `dpa-baa-templates.md`.

If `get_doc(page: enum)` only takes one page name at a time, the model has to (a) know all five page names exist, and (b) decide to call the tool five times to assemble a complete answer. That's the same routing gap the compliance question exposes: a freeform-string parameter means the model is guessing page names, and even with the parameter typed as a `Literal`/enum listing all five, there's no guarantee the model makes all five calls rather than one or two and answering as if that's complete — a partial-as-final failure, the exact pattern the MCP honesty work already flagged repeatedly elsewhere in this codebase.

Two ways to fix that gap, not mutually exclusive:
1. **Make the page list discoverable in the tool's own docstring/schema** — enumerate all valid pages (including all five compliance ones) as a `Literal` type, not freeform text, so the model sees them as an explicit menu rather than having to guess.
2. **Add a `list_doc_pages()` tool** (or have an invalid `page` value return the valid list) so a broad question like "what compliance mechanisms exist" naturally resolves to "list pages → see 5 compliance ones → fetch each" — same self-correcting shape DataQ already uses elsewhere (e.g., an unrecognized argument's error message doubling as guidance).

Worth testing empirically rather than assuming, per the "a routing score isn't the finding" lesson — the interesting failure mode isn't "does it ever answer," it's "does it fetch all five or stop at one and present a partial answer as complete."
So what do you suggest?

Two tools, not one: `list_doc_pages()` (returns page names + categories, e.g. grouping the five compliance pages together) and `get_doc(page: Literal[...])` for the actual fetch. That makes discovery explicit rather than betting on the model guessing a freeform string or noticing every enum value buried in one docstring — same self-correcting shape DataQ already uses elsewhere (an unknown value's error doubles as the menu).

Main tradeoff: it's two tool calls for a broad question like the compliance one instead of one, and two more entries in the MCP tool list to maintain — but given how consistently "partial answer presented as complete" has been the real failure mode in this codebase's MCP work, I'd take that over a single opaque `get_doc` call that silently under-fetches.

Want me to scope this as a GitHub issue, or are you still deciding between A/B/C first?
Does the list_doc need to be exposed to user or can it be a private method?

It doesn't have to be — it can be a private helper. The key insight: if `get_doc`'s `page` parameter is typed as a `Literal[...]`/enum, the MCP tool schema itself lists every valid value to the model on every turn (that's just how JSON-schema enums render in the tool definition) — no separate call needed for discovery. `list_doc_pages()` only earns its own registered-tool status if either the catalog is too large/dynamic to hardcode as an enum, or you need to convey more than a name (descriptions, grouping) that an enum alone can't carry.

Given DataQ's docs corpus is a handful of static files, I'd skip the second tool: keep a private page registry, build the `Literal` from it, and use **prefixed names** for grouping (e.g. `compliance/sub-processors`, `compliance/dpia-input-sheet`) so the model can see from the enum alone that five compliance pages exist without a lookup call. Simpler surface, one tool, same discoverability.
But if we are listing the pages in list_doc, Instead of fetching it dynamically, it will create a drift. Correct? how we are going to handle this?

Correct — a hand-maintained list is exactly the failure mode this codebase has hit before (the MCP tool-count doc headings drifting from the actual body list, `mcp_gates.GATES` existing specifically because a hand-typed gate list silently went stale). Same shape here: someone adds a new page under `docs/site/`, forgets to update the hardcoded enum, and the tool can't see it.

Fix: don't hand-maintain it — **derive the page catalog from `docs/site/` itself at server startup**, the same "declare as data, don't hand-count" pattern already used for `GATES`. Concretely:
- Glob `docs/site/**/*.md` once at import time, building `{slug: path}` (directory structure gives you category grouping for free — `compliance/sub-processors.md` → category `compliance`).
- Build the tool's parameter validation and any enum/description text from that scan, not typed twice by hand.
- Skip Python's static `Literal[...]` type for this (it can't be populated dynamically without fighting mypy, a hard CI gate here) — use plain `page: str` with runtime validation against the scanned set, and an "unknown page, valid pages are: [...]" error that's itself always current since it's built from the same scan.

That removes the drift surface entirely — there's nothing to keep in sync because there's only one copy of the truth (the filesystem), and the tool reads it fresh at process start rather than at "whenever someone remembered to update the list."
Okay. If we are to implement this, what changes are required?

Concrete change list, six pieces:

**1. `backend/Dockerfile`** — real gap I just confirmed: the backend image only `COPY`s `backend/` and `pyproject.toml`; `docs/site/` never makes it into the container. Needs `COPY docs/site ./docs/site` in the runtime stage, or the tool works locally and 404s/errors in prod. This is exactly the "merged ≠ deployed, deployed ≠ works" class this repo has been bitten by before.

**2. New module `backend/app/mcp/docs_catalog.py`**
- `DOCS_ROOT` resolved relative to the repo root (`Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "docs" / "site"`) so it works identically in the local checkout and the container.
- Scan `**/*.md` once, build `{slug: {path, category, title}}` — slug = relative path w/o extension (e.g. `compliance/sub-processors`), category = the leading directory, title = the file's first `#` heading.
- `list_pages()` and `read_page(slug)` (raises with the valid-slug list on a miss).

**3. One new tool in `server.py`: `get_doc(page: str)`** — thin wrapper over `docs_catalog.read_page`, `@mcp.tool`, read-only, no suite scoping (docs are workspace-agnostic and already public — same "no per-resource gate" bucket as `list_suites`). Docstring needs the honesty framing this codebase already applies: states it returns the page verbatim (not a summary), and that an unrecognized `page` returns the current valid list.

**4. `tests/support/mcp_gates.py`** — add `"get_doc": "read"`.

**5. Tests** — a small `test_mcp_docs.py`: valid slug round-trips, invalid slug's error lists real pages, and one test asserting the catalog actually finds the five compliance pages (catches a glob-pattern bug, not catalog drift — drift is structurally impossible since it's a live scan).

**6. Doc-count references** — `docs/site/mcp-setup.md`, `docs/site/changelog.md`, and CLAUDE.md's tool-count line all currently say some N tools; this adds one, and per standing practice those counts should derive from `GATES` rather than be hand-bumped again.

Then the usual: GitHub issue, PR, `/code-review` (I'd specifically loop in `mcp-honesty-reviewer` given it's a new tool's docstring), and a deploy check that the built image actually contains `docs/site` before calling it done.

gh issue create \
  --title "MCP: expose curated docs via a get_doc tool (best-practices, compliance, feature-matrix)" \
  --label "enhancement" \
  --milestone "v1.2 Backlog" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

`/mcp`'s 46 tools are all backend-data reads/mutations (suites, checks, runs, connections, assets, incidents, ...). None of them expose the published user-facing docs (`docs/site/`, public on GH Pages). A question like *"what are best practices for creating a suite/check?"* or *"what compliance mechanisms does DataQ support?"* has no path to the actual docs content — the model answers from training data / tool docstrings only, not from `best-practices.md` or the five `compliance/*.md` pages.

## Decision (from design discussion)

- **Tool, not resource.** MCP resources are passive — most clients don't auto-fetch them based on conversation content, so a client answering an NL question wouldn't reliably reach the doc. A tool goes through the same routing mechanism the other 46 tools already use (model sees description, decides to call).
- **`get_doc(page: str)`**, scoped to a curated allowlist of user-facing pages — not the whole `docs/site/` tree. **ADRs are explicitly excluded**: they're contributor/design-rationale docs, not the audience asking these questions, and 40 extra slugs would mostly add noise to the exact discovery problem this tool exists to solve. Same reasoning excludes `architecture.md`. In scope: `best-practices.md`, `feature-matrix.md`, `security.md`, `getting-started.md`, `mcp-setup.md`, `compliance/*.md` (5 pages).
- **Catalog built from a live filesystem scan at import time, not a hand-maintained list** — same "declare as data, don't hand-count" lesson as `tests/support/mcp_gates.GATES` (which exists precisely because a hand-typed list drifted before). Scanning is scoped to the curated allowlist directories/files above, not a blanket `**/*.md`.
- Unknown `page` argument returns a clear error listing the current valid pages (self-correcting, same shape used elsewhere in this MCP surface).

## Scope of change

1. **`backend/Dockerfile`** — the runtime image currently only `COPY`s `backend/` + `pyproject.toml`; `docs/site/` is never copied in. Needs a `COPY docs/site ./docs/site` (or a scoped subset copy) or this 404s/errors in every deployed environment despite working locally.
2. **New module `backend/app/mcp/docs_catalog.py`** — resolves `docs/site` relative to repo root, scans the curated allowlist, exposes `list_pages()` / `read_page(slug)`.
3. **New tool in `backend/app/mcp/server.py`: `get_doc(page: str)`** — `@mcp.tool`, read-only, no suite scoping (docs are workspace-agnostic and already public — same "no per-resource gate" bucket as `list_suites`). Docstring follows this surface's honesty conventions: states it returns the page verbatim (no summarization), and that an unrecognized `page` returns the current valid list.
4. **`tests/support/mcp_gates.py`** — add `"get_doc": "read"`.
5. **Tests** — valid-slug round-trip, invalid-slug error content, and a check that the scan actually finds the known compliance pages (catches a glob/path bug, not "drift" — drift is structurally ruled out by scanning live).
6. **Tool-count references** — `docs/site/mcp-setup.md`, `docs/site/changelog.md`, and CLAUDE.md's MCP tool-count line all need the +1; per standing practice, derive the count from `GATES` rather than hand-bump again.
7. **Verify the built image actually contains `docs/site`** before calling this deployed — don't rely on CI green alone (this repo's own "merged ≠ deployed, deployed ≠ works" lesson).

## Out of scope (for now)

- ADRs and `architecture.md` — deliberately excluded, see above.
- A `list_doc_pages()` companion tool — not needed initially; `page` is typed so the JSON-schema enum already advertises the full curated page list to the model on every turn.
EOF
)"

13

16	  2. A page added under `docs/site/` should be *findable*: either in `nav`, or
17	     matching PUBLISHED_UNLINKED below (today: ADRs — reachable from prose and
18	     the ADR index; forty sidebar entries would bury the guides). A page in

20	     as an explicit-decision prompt, not a publication risk.
21	"""
22	
23	from __future__ import annotations
24	
25	import re
26	from pathlib import Path
27	
28	SITE = Path("docs/site")
29	MKDOCS = Path("mkdocs.yml")
30	
31	# Published deliberately, but not in the nav. Glob patterns, relative to docs/site/.
32	PUBLISHED_UNLINKED = ("adr/*.md",)
33	
34	
35	def _nav_entries(text: str) -> set[str]:
36	    """Every `*.md` mentioned in the nav block.
37	
38	    Deliberately a regex over the nav section rather than a YAML parse: mkdocs.yml
39	    carries mkdocs-material's `!!python/name:` tags, which the safe loader refuses
40	    (the repo's own check-yaml hook passes `--unsafe` for the same reason).
41	    """
42	    m = re.search(r"^nav:\n(.*?)(?=^\S)", text, re.M | re.S)
43	    return set(re.findall(r"([A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.md)", m.group(1))) if m else set()
44	
45	
46	def main() -> int:
47	    if not MKDOCS.is_file():
48	        print("mkdocs.yml not found — run from the repo root")
49	        return 1
50	    text = MKDOCS.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
51	
52	    m = re.search(r"^docs_dir:\s*(\S+)", text, re.M)
53	    if not m or m.group(1) != "docs/site":
54	        print(
55	            "Docs publication check FAILED — `docs_dir` must be `docs/site`.\n\n"
56	            f"mkdocs.yml currently has: docs_dir: {m.group(1) if m else '<absent>'}\n\n"
57	            "The docs/site/ split makes LOCATION the publication decision: internal\n"
58	            "planning docs live at docs/ and publish only if deliberately moved into\n"
59	            "docs/site/. Pointing docs_dir back at docs/ would publish every internal\n"
60	            "file (ops log included) in one line."
61	        )
62	        return 1
63	
64	    if re.search(r"^exclude_docs:", text, re.M):
65	        print(
66	            "Docs publication check FAILED — `exclude_docs` is back in mkdocs.yml.\n"
67	            "With docs_dir at docs/site there is nothing to exclude; an exclude list\n"
68	            "reintroduces the publish-by-default model this layout replaced. Move the\n"
69	            "file out of docs/site/ instead."
70	        )
71	        return 1
72	
73	    nav = _nav_entries(text)
74	    unlinked = {
75	        p.relative_to(SITE).as_posix() for pat in PUBLISHED_UNLINKED for p in SITE.glob(pat)
76	    }
77	    undeclared = sorted(
78	        rel
79	        for p in SITE.rglob("*.md")
80	        if (rel := p.relative_to(SITE).as_posix()) not in nav and rel not in unlinked
81	    )

95	    )

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Published docs never cite issue IDs, PR numbers, or link to unpublished docs.

CONTRIBUTING.md rule 41: everything under `docs/site/` (the mkdocs `docs_dir`,
built to the public GitHub Pages site) is read by people with no access to this
repo's issue tracker. A `#1234` or an `.../issues/1234` / `.../pull/1234` link
is internal project-tracking noise to that reader — state the behavior or
decision itself, not the ticket that produced it. Bare GitHub issue/PR
shorthand is never how DataQ's own ADRs cite each other either (that's always
"ADR 0012" or a same-directory `0012-*.md` link, never `#0012`), so this check
needs no ADR-to-ADR exception.

A published page also must never link to an unpublished internal doc
(README/CONTRIBUTING/CLAUDE.md, docs/progress*.md, docs/retro*.md,
docs/ops-log.md) — those aren't reachable from the site, so the link is dead
weight for a reader outside the repo.

(Minimizing an ordinary page's links into docs/site/adr/, and minimizing an
ADR's own links to the PR that shipped it, are judgment calls a script can't
make — that's a review-time check, not this one.)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SITE = Path("docs/site")

ISSUE_OR_PR_SHORTHAND = re.compile(r"#[0-9]{2,5}\b")
ISSUE_OR_PR_LINK = re.compile(r"github\.com/[^)\s]*?/(?:issues|pull)/[0-9]+")

UNPUBLISHED_DOC_LINK = re.compile(
    r"\]\([^)]*\b("
    r"README\.md"
    r"|CONTRIBUTING\.md"
    r"|CLAUDE\.md"
    r"|docs/progress[^)]*\.md"
    r"|docs/retro[^)]*\.md"
    r"|docs/ops-log\.md"
    r")\)"
)


def main() -> int:
    if not SITE.is_dir():
        print(f"{SITE} not found — run from the repo root")
        return 1

    violations: list[str] = []
    for path in sorted(SITE.rglob("*.md")):
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for lineno, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
            for pattern, label in (
                (ISSUE_OR_PR_SHORTHAND, "issue/PR shorthand"),
                (ISSUE_OR_PR_LINK, "issue/PR link"),
                (UNPUBLISHED_DOC_LINK, "link to an unpublished internal doc"),
            ):
                for m in pattern.finditer(line):
                    violations.append(f"  {path}:{lineno}: {label} — {m.group(0)!r}")

    if not violations:
        return 0

    print("Docs reference check FAILED — published pages must not cite tickets")
    print("or link to unpublished docs (CONTRIBUTING.md rule 41):\n")
    print("\n".join(violations))
    print(
        "\nRewrite the sentence to state the behavior/decision itself instead of\n"
        "pointing at the ticket, or drop the link to the unpublished doc."
    )
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
